body.q: A business owner takes goods from the business inventory for personal use and does not record the transaction. Which accounting concept has been ignored?
body.why: The business entity concept requires the owner's personal transactions to be kept separate from those of the business, so goods taken must be recorded as drawings.

body.q: A trader values closing inventory at cost price rather than at the higher selling price. Which accounting concept is being applied?
body.why: Prudence means profits and assets should not be overstated, so inventory is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value.

body.q: A business has always used the reducing balance method to depreciate its vehicles. This year it uses the straight-line method purely to show a higher profit. Which concept has been broken?
body.why: Consistency requires the same accounting methods to be used from one period to the next so that results can be compared.

body.q: Which of the following could NOT be recorded in the accounts of a business because of the money measurement concept?
body.why: Money measurement means only items that can be expressed in monetary terms are recorded, and the quality of staff cannot be given a reliable money value.

body.q: A business buys a machine for $20 000. A year later a similar machine costs $24 000. The machine remains in the accounts at $20 000 less depreciation. Which concept is being applied?
body.why: Historic cost means assets are recorded at the price originally paid rather than at their current market value.

body.q: A business records a sale when the goods are delivered and the invoice is sent to the customer, even though payment is received the following month. Which concept does this show?
body.why: Realisation states that revenue is recognised when goods or services are supplied, not when the cash is received.

body.q: A business pays $1 200 in December for insurance covering the following year. Which concept requires the expense to be shown in the following year's income statement?
body.why: The matching concept requires expenses to be recorded in the same period as the revenue they helped to earn, regardless of when they were paid.

body.q: A business buys a stapler for $4 and records it as an expense rather than as a non-current asset. Which concept justifies this treatment?
body.why: Materiality allows insignificant items to be treated in the simplest way, as the amount is too small to affect decisions.

body.q: The accountant of a business prepares the financial statements assuming that the business will continue to trade for the foreseeable future. Which concept is being applied?
body.why: The going concern concept assumes the business will continue to operate, so assets are not valued as if they were about to be sold off.

body.q: A business purchases a computer on credit. It records an increase in non-current assets and an increase in payables. Which concept does this illustrate?
body.why: The dual aspect concept states that every transaction has two effects on the accounts, so each debit entry has a matching credit entry.
